nodes.label: Insufficient-balance payment status (applied out-of-band, never in a repo migration)
Gotcha: this repo ships stub migrations - the live schema, not supabase/migrations/, is the source of truth
Customer-ledger charge category taxonomy (what a line on a customer's balance can be)
One money-category vocabulary shared by the customer ledger, the P&L and payment allocation
Gotcha: singular/plural aliases ('InitialFee' vs 'Initial Fees', 'Fine' vs 'Fines') are both still legal - historical rows force it
P&L entry category taxonomy (operator-side profit and loss buckets)
P&L-only buckets (Acquisition, Finance, Disposal, Plates) have no ledger counterpart - the two taxonomies overlap but are not equal
A payment can only ever post to the ledger once
Rationale: the partial unique index is deliberately used as a database-level lock for apply-payment idempotency, not merely as a constraint
Which charge categories a payment is meant to settle, carried on the payment row itself
Rationale: allocation targets moved out of browser localStorage because Stripe webhooks and other tabs could not read it
Per-vehicle opt-out of the daily / weekly / monthly booking durations
Rationale: all three toggles default true so every pre-existing vehicle stays fully bookable
Portal staff must record acceptance of the tenant's privacy policy and terms
Consent is unique per (user, policy, version) - bumping tenants.privacy_policy_version or terms_version re-prompts every staff member
IP address and user-agent are captured so an acceptance can be evidenced later
Users may only read and insert their own acceptance; head_admin/admin and super admins get read-only visibility across the tenant
New tenants are 24/7-open by default rather than having to configure working hours before they can take bookings
Gotcha: changing a column DEFAULT only affects rows inserted afterwards - existing tenants keep whatever value they had
Rentals are published to supabase_realtime so signing/status changes reach open portal and booking screens without a refetch
Gotcha: comments and columns still say DocuSign although the e-signature provider is BoldSign (see rentals.docusign_envelope_id)
The ALTER PUBLICATION is wrapped in a pg_publication_tables existence check so the migration is safe to re-run
Weekend and holiday surcharge pricing configured per tenant
Rationale: dynamic pricing only applies to the daily tier (<7 days); weekly and monthly rates are unaffected
weekend_days stores JS Date day numbers (0=Sun..6=Sat), coupling the DB value to client-side date code
Named holiday date ranges with their own surcharge, optionally recurring annually
A holiday can exclude vehicles inline via excluded_vehicle_ids, duplicating what vehicle_pricing_overrides 'excluded' also expresses
Per-vehicle override of a weekend or holiday rule: fixed price, custom percent, or excluded
vehicle_pricing_overrides has no tenant_id - its RLS derives tenancy by joining to vehicles, so a vehicle row move silently re-homes the override
Gotcha: the FOR ALL 'manage' policies specify USING but no WITH CHECK, so inserts/updates are not re-validated against the tenant predicate
A single timestamp on the tenant marking that its policies were accepted, separate from the per-user acceptance rows
Signing emails and the signing page carry the tenant's own BoldSign brand
Tenant-wide 'how to use the lockbox' text appended to every lockbox email/SMS/WhatsApp, on top of the per-vehicle location note
Minimum rental duration can be expressed in hours, enabling sub-day rentals
Total minimum = (min_rental_days * 24) + min_rental_hours - two columns must be read together, never one alone
Gotcha: the migration rewrites every min_rental_days = 1 to 0, silently erasing tenants who deliberately wanted a 1-day minimum
Customers and rentals can be flagged as gig-economy driving (Uber/Lyft), which changes eligibility and pricing treatment
Per-customer proof-of-gig-work image uploads
Gotcha: the guest-checkout anon policies use WITH CHECK (true) / USING (true), so the anon key can read and write every tenant's gig-driver images
The gig-driver-images bucket is public and grants PUBLIC delete on storage.objects, so anyone can remove another tenant's uploads
Rationale: uploads must work during guest checkout, before the uploader has any authenticated identity
Reviews run operator-to-customer: portal staff rate the renter after a completed rental (internal, never customer-facing)
A review may be skipped; the CHECK makes rating mandatory only when is_skipped is false, so 'not yet reviewed' and 'declined to review' stay distinguishable
One AI-generated reputation summary per customer per tenant, holding the rolling average and review count
Gotcha: reviewer_id is NOT NULL yet declared ON DELETE SET NULL - deleting an app_user will raise instead of orphaning the review
Gotcha: the policy named 'Service role can manage summaries' is USING (true) WITH CHECK (true) with no TO clause, so any role can write summaries
Each tenant runs BoldSign in test or live mode, mirroring the per-tenant Stripe dual-mode pattern
rentals.boldsign_mode records which mode issued the agreement so the webhook can later pick the matching API key
Breaking rename: boldsign_brand_id becomes boldsign_live_brand_id and a boldsign_test_brand_id is added, because BoldSign brands are environment-specific
Per-agreement metered billing: one row per live e-sign agreement sent, at $1.00 each
Subscription invoices carry base_amount / usage_amount / usage_quantity so a tenant can see fixed fee versus metered usage
stripe_event_id is stored so local usage rows can be reconciled against Stripe meter events
Gotcha: the comment claims only service_role may insert usage, but the policy is WITH CHECK (true) with no TO clause
Only live-mode agreements are metered - test-mode signing is free, which is why boldsign_mode has to be recorded
A rental can carry several signed agreements - the original plus one per extension
period_start_date / period_end_date scope each agreement to the stretch of the rental it covers
Existing single-agreement state is backfilled out of the rentals row (docusign_envelope_id, envelope_* timestamps) guarded by a NOT EXISTS re-run check
Gotcha: the legacy agreement columns on rentals are not dropped, so agreement state now lives in two places and can diverge
Mileage allowance is set per booking tier (daily / weekly / monthly) instead of one flat number
Breaking change: the old allowed_mileage column is copied into monthly_mileage and then dropped - every reader must migrate in the same release
Tenant-specific logo on the portal login page, distinct from the sidebar/booking logo
Rationale: auth_logo_url only affects the login screen; sidebar and booking keep reading logo_url, so the two must not be conflated
Gotcha: the migration UPDATEs one named customer (slug 'rbvs') with a hardcoded storage URL - per-tenant data in schema history
One RPC returns every portal tab's headline metrics for a tenant, so the AI assistant can answer numeric questions without table access
Rationale: every status comparison is wrapped in LOWER() because status strings are stored with inconsistent casing across tables
Rationale: the aggregate is split into seven jsonb_build_object calls and merged with || to stay under Postgres' 100-argument limit
This one function touches ~15 tables, so almost any schema or status-vocabulary change silently degrades the assistant's numbers
Gotcha: the function is SECURITY DEFINER and trusts its p_tenant_id argument with no auth check, so it must never be exposed to an untrusted caller
A rental's insurance is either the original policy or a supplemental policy covering the gap opened by an extension
Rationale: extending a rental past the original cover period leaves an uninsured window that a second Bonzah policy must fill
Authenticated customers can read the Bonzah policies attached to them, making insurance visible in the booking-side customer portal
Rationale: customers authenticate through customer_users, not app_users, so the usual get_user_tenant_id() RLS helper yields nothing and policies must join customer_users on auth.uid()
Tenants pre-buy platform credits and every billable action draws them down
Rationale: the credit wallet explicitly replaces Stripe metered billing - the e-sign usage log's model is superseded
A single tariff table prices each billable service in credits (e-sign 7, SMS 2, licence verification 31), editable without a deploy
Purchasable credit bundles with bonus credits, an 'is_popular' merchandising flag and their own Stripe price
Deduction locks the wallet row FOR UPDATE, checks balance, debits and writes the ledger entry in one transaction so concurrent actions cannot overdraw
Test-mode actions cost 0 credits yet still write a transaction row (auto-creating the wallet), so test traffic stays visible without billing
Gotcha: deduct_credits returns auto_refill_needed but never refills - the caller must act on the signal or the wallet just runs dry
credit_transactions is an append-only ledger that snapshots balance_after on every row, so balance history is reconstructable
CHECK (balance >= 0) backs up the in-function balance test, so even a buggy caller cannot drive a wallet negative
Gotcha: add_credits folds 'gift' into lifetime_purchased alongside real purchases, so that column overstates revenue
add_credits creates the wallet on demand, so tenants never need an explicit provisioning step - but deduct_credits does not, and fails closed instead

hyperedges.label: E-signature lifecycle: tenant mode -> agreement row -> live push -> metered/credit charge
Payment posting pipeline: allocation targets -> idempotent ledger post -> shared category vocabulary -> P&L
Extending a rental ripples through agreements, insurance cover, mileage tiers and ledger categories
